newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar easier in Tokyo after peaking above 116 yen.
newsitem.headline: Dollar easier in Tokyo after peaking above 116 yen.

text.p: The dollar drifted down against the yen by late afternoon Friday as long holders unwound positions after the greenback failed to stay above 116 yen.

Dollar sales by U.S. hedge funds and yen-buying in crosses by Japanese exporters slightly depressed the trend of the dollar/yen. But it was supported by Japanese trust banks buying, along with life insurers' bids around 115.20/30 yen.

The greenback rose as high as 116.23 yen on purchases by trust banks and commercial buying at Japan's local fixing in early trade. But the dollar's ascent paused amid exporter offers on the upside and a lack of trading incentives to prompt follow-through purchases, dealers said.
After the dollar eased off its peak, operators in Tokyo concentrated on position-squaring before the long weekend in Japan and ahead of U.S. trade data due out at 1230 GMT.
"Although the impact of U.S. trade data is expected to be limited, it'll be too risky to carry long positions in large volume," a European bank dealer said.
The dollar closed at 115.85/95 yen and 1.7915/25 marks in New York on Thursday.

The dollar came under slight downard pressure against the yen due to yen purchases by Japanese exporters, including electric firms and car makers, spotted in crosses especially European currencies, dealers said.
U.S. fund operators were forced them to dump the mark against the yen in the afternoon after it failed to hit 65.05/10 yen, where stop-loss buy orders were lined up.
At 0646 GMT, the mark stood at 64.50/60 yen compared with 64.72 yen in early Tokyo trade.
With the underlying bull trend in the dollar against the mark intact, the dollar/yen had more potential to test its upper side in the short term, dealers said.

"The dollar is more likely to test a high of 116.40 yen once more," said Yoh Nihei, a manager at Sakura Bank. "But if the dollar fails to break above that level, then the dollar should stay in the 115 yen level."
The dollar hit a high of 116.40 in New York on Wednesday.
Dealers said exporters were placing selling orders at around 116.50 yen, but that they may withdraw their orders as stop-loss buy orders were also spotted at that level.
Singapore dealers said the dollar was seen in demand against the mark, but was stuck in a tight range against the German currency in Asia.
Some players were closely looking towards the French budget audit scheduled for Monday.
French government sources said the audit will show a budget deficit of around 3.5 to 3.6 percent of the GDP, compared with the 3.0 percent forecast in the 1997 Finance Act.
Despite recent moves by German monetary officials to talk up the mark, the German currency is still under pressure amid lingering worries about a weak European single currency.
Dealers said the market will be watching U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony next week.
"The market may want to see how U.S. stocks and Treasury prices move in response to Greenspan's testimony," a Japanese trust bank dealer said.
Japanese financial markets will be closed on Monday for a national holiday. ---Singapore newsroom +65-870-3080 ---Chikafumi Hodo, Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-8785
